items.stem: "Barauni is called a market-based refinery." Examine this statement with reference to conventional and non-conventional energy resources.
items.answer: The statement is valid. It was set up near the market for petroleum products rather than near an oil field.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (it was set up near the market for petroleum products rather than near an oil field.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:

Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It is used in making steel and ferro-manganese alloys.
items.markingKey: (b) It is used in making steel and ferro-manganese alloys.
options: It was set up near the market for petroleum products rather than near an oil field.
It is used in making steel and ferro-manganese alloys.
It has excellent insulating properties and can be split into thin sheets.
They are renewable, cleaner and reduce dependence on exhaustible fossil fuels.

items.stem:
Statement: The north-eastern plateau region is rich in minerals.

items.answer: It contains Chota Nagpur and the Odisha plateau with iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.
items.markingKey: (c) It contains Chota Nagpur and the Odisha plateau with iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.
options: It has a high tidal range.
Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.
It contains Chota Nagpur and the Odisha plateau with iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about conservation of mineral resources is correct?
items.answer: Alternative energy sources such as solar, wind, tidal and geothermal can replace exhaustible minerals.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: Conservation means judicious and planned use of minerals. Recycling reduces the demand for fresh ores. Minerals are non-renewable and take millions of years to form.
options: Alternative energy sources such as solar, wind, tidal and geothermal can replace exhaustible minerals.
Recycling scrap metals increases the demand for new ores.
Minerals are renewable resources that form quickly.
Conservation means stopping the use of all minerals.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on types and distribution of minerals in India and answer the questions that follow.
"The south-western plateau region extends over Karnataka, Goa and the contiguous Tamil Nadu uplands and Kerala. The north-western belt extends along the Aravalli in Rajasthan and part of Gujarat. The Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten."
(i) Copper and zinc are mainly found in which mineral belt? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'metallic minerals' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The north-eastern plateau region is rich in minerals. (1)
items.answer: (i) The north-western region (Aravalli) (ii) Minerals from which metals are obtained, divided into ferrous and non-ferrous minerals. (iii) It contains Chota Nagpur and the Odisha plateau with iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The north-western region (Aravalli) (ii) Minerals from which metals are obtained, divided into ferrous and non-ferrous minerals. (iii) It contains Chota Nagpur and the Odisha plateau with iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica.

items.stem: What is meant by 'mica' in the context of ferrous, non-ferrous and non-metallic minerals?
items.answer: A non-metallic mineral used in the electrical and electronics industries because of its insulating properties.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: mica correctly explained as a non-metallic mineral used in the electrical and electronics industries because of its insulating properties.

items.stem:
Statement: Recycling of metals helps conservation.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.
items.markingKey: (a) Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.
options: Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.
It was set up near the market for petroleum products rather than near an oil field.
Minerals are non-renewable and their reserves are limited.
The old crystalline rocks of the plateau contain rich deposits of metallic minerals.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about conventional and non-conventional energy resources is correct?
items.answer: About 80 per cent of India's coal deposits are of bituminous type and are of non-coking grade.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: They are renewable and inexhaustible. It is obtained from the monazite sands of Kerala. Jharia is the largest coalfield, in Jharkhand; Digboi is an oil field in Assam.

items.stem: The following statement about conventional and non-conventional energy resources is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Non-conventional sources of energy are exhaustible."
items.answer: They are renewable and inexhaustible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They are renewable and inexhaustible.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on conservation of mineral resources and answer the questions that follow.
"Exports of strategic and scarce minerals should be reduced to keep reserves for future use. Minerals are non-renewable and take millions of years to form. Substitutes for scarce metals can reduce their consumption."
(i) Which of these helps conserve mineral resources? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'substitution' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Recycling of metals helps conservation. (1)
items.answer: (i) Recycling scrap metals (ii) The use of alternative materials in place of scarce minerals. (iii) Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Recycling scrap metals (ii) The use of alternative materials in place of scarce minerals. (iii) Scrap metals can be reused instead of mining fresh ore.

items.stem: The following statement about types and distribution of minerals in India is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Most metallic minerals of India occur in the northern plains."
items.answer: They occur mostly in the peninsular plateau region in old crystalline rocks.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They occur mostly in the peninsular plateau region in old crystalline rocks.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about types and distribution of minerals in India is correct?
items.answer: The north-eastern plateau region covers Chota Nagpur in Jharkhand, the Odisha plateau, West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Coal is a non-metallic mineral and a fuel. They are found mainly in the Aravalli region of Rajasthan and Gujarat. They occur mostly in the peninsular plateau region in old crystalline rocks.

The north-eastern plateau region covers Chota Nagpur in Jharkhand, the Odisha plateau, West Bengal and parts of Chhattisgarh.

items.stem: Bauxite is the ore of:
items.answer: aluminium
items.markingKey: (b) aluminium.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about conventional and non-conventional energy resources:
I. About 80 per cent of India's coal deposits are of bituminous type and are of non-coking grade.
II. Oil refineries are of two types: field-based, such as Digboi, and market-based, such as Barauni.
III. Non-conventional sources of energy are exhaustible.

items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: They are renewable and inexhaustible.

items.answer: The judicious and planned use of mineral resources so that they last longer and serve future generations

items.stem:
Read the following extract on ferrous, non-ferrous and non-metallic minerals and answer the questions that follow.
"Iron ore in India is mainly haematite and magnetite. Odisha and Jharkhand have large deposits of iron ore, and Chhattisgarh has the Bailadila mines. Copper is mined in Singhbhum in Jharkhand, Balaghat in Madhya Pradesh and Khetri in Rajasthan."
(i) Which state is the largest producer of bauxite in India? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'haematite' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Manganese is important for the iron and steel industry. (1)
items.answer: (i) Odisha (ii) The best quality iron ore, with a high iron content. (iii) It is used in making steel and ferro-manganese alloys.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Odisha (ii) The best quality iron ore, with a high iron content. (iii) It is used in making steel and ferro-manganese alloys.
